briefing.body: We have a functioning device. The build is packed, and the screen is showing detections. Current action items: Ridwan is programming CCS and UniFlash for better person detection with custom firmware. Fawaz is getting LoRa working on the ESP32, along with heat-set inserts and the 3D model. Josh is syncing LoRa data with the cloud for a live dashboard with device data and identifiers. Faris is handling digital signal processing and the config file after Ridwan, focused on isolating targets and improving accuracy, including AirTag-like tracking technology. Faizan is working on DLP and display graphics and drivers, targeting 30 to 60 FPS, also toward AirTag-like tracking. All tasks are tracked on our Jira Kanban board.
briefing.author: Joshua Zachariah

decisions.decision: A live cloud backend is a core goal of Hera Beacon
decisions.reason: A live AWS IoT Core backend is part of the core scope, not a later add on. This supersedes the framing in the Sep 17 POC dashboard entry, which deferred cloud work until multiple deployed units needed centralized aggregation. Following Dr. Skinner's guidance, hardware remains the near term priority, so cloud work is sequenced behind getting the handheld unit working. Real time data from the handheld unit reaching a command center is central to what Hera Beacon is for, so presenting it as a simulated concept undersold the project.
TI radar module is confirmed. ESP32 / XIAO is the working track for Senior Design 1, and Qualcomm's Arduino UNO Q is under parallel evaluation. The final board is not committed.
Committed for Senior Design 1: a sub board and module stack, not a custom bare microprocessor board. The approach for the final product is still open, driven partly by sourcing constraints.
Open. Pending empirical RF testing through rebar reinforced concrete.

decisions.decision: Hera Beacon is handheld, not throwable
decisions.reason: The team's POC direction, an individual display on the device itself, confirmed handheld as the working design. Reasoning: physical rescue always requires a responder to eventually approach the survivor directly, so an operator carried device does not introduce a fundamentally new category of risk beyond what rescue already requires. Open item for testing: detection range and signal penetration through debris draw on the same power budget, so whether the device's realistic standoff distance provides a meaningful safety margin over close range needs empirical validation. This is part of the RF and rebar characterization already planned.

decisions.decision: Use TI IWR6843AOPEVM for core sensing
decisions.reason: Chosen over designing a custom RF front end. Millimeter wave RF front end design requires specialized test equipment and multi week PCB fabrication cycles, and a single layout error can leave the device with no working sensor at all. Using qualified TI radar silicon lets the team put its engineering effort into vital sign extraction, system integration, and the handheld unit itself, which mirrors how commercial radar vital sign products are typically built.

decisions.decision: POC dashboard runs locally, not through AWS
decisions.reason: Standing up real AWS infrastructure, device certificates, IAM permissions, an actual cloud connected dashboard, is genuine additional engineering work that does not serve what the POC is actually meant to prove, that the sensors and display pipeline work. A local dashboard the ESP32 serves on its own WiFi network proves the same core capability and is faster to build, which matters given the deadline. AWS remains the settled choice for the real fleet system later, once multiple deployed units actually need centralized data aggregation.

decisions.decision: Use AWS as the cloud provider for Hera
decisions.reason: Google discontinued its equivalent service, Cloud IoT Core, back in 2023, so AWS is the only one of the two that still has a real, purpose built product for connecting and managing sensor devices at all. The team also already has direct AWS IoT Core experience from a prior project.

decisions.decision: How do we get data off the device in remote locations where WiFi is unavailable and cellular is limited?
decisions.reason: Open. Need a connectivity and offload plan for field deployments with weak or no network. Update, Oct 5, 2026: LoRa is now the leading candidate and is under active range testing. Still open, not committed.
